title: Salt of the Earth! Ye Virtuous Few
description: Salt of the Earth! Ye Virtuous Few in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anna Laetitia Barbauld wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 768 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Ye are the Salt of the Earth."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Salt of the earth! ye vir-tuous few Who sea-son hu-man kind; Light of the world! whose cheer-ing ray Il-lumes the realms of mind.

lines: Salt of the earth! ye virtuous few
Light of the world! whose cheering ray
Where misery spreads her deepest shade
From your blest lips the balm proceeds
Yours is the large expansive thought,
Exile and chains to you are dear,
Proceed! your race of glory run,
You come commissioned from on high,

licence: Public domain: Anna Laetitia Barbauld died in 1825.
credits: Words by Anna Laetitia Barbauld (1743–1825), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
